34. **Misprints and scansion (aeneid-040).** Published as printed in `t` (t must match the pinned source), each note opening with the print's reading and `l`/`i` giving the correct marks (rule 5b); closing marks that Greenough prints joined to the next word stand at the head of the next unit's `t` (as aeneid-037), because the build refuses a unit that ends on `”` against the next word. Correction and place:
- 6.45 `virgo. “Poscere fata` / 6.46 `“tempus ait; deus, ecce, deus! ”Cui`: should read `virgo, “Poscere fata tempus” ait; “deus, ecce, deus!” Cui` (full stop for comma after `virgo`; the opening mark before `tempus` should be a closing mark after it; no opening mark before the second `deus`; closing mark joined to `Cui`). Units: VI.45 (opens `The print has…`), VI.46 `deus, ecce, deus!`, and `”Cui talia fanti`.
- 6.51-52 `“Cessas in vota precesque, / “Tros ait Aenea?`: should read `“Cessas in vota precesque, Tros” ait “Aenea? Cessas?…` (the opening mark before `Tros` should be a closing mark after it, and a new opening mark belongs before `Aenea`). Unit VI.51.
- 6.53 `domus. ”Et talia fata`: should read `domus.” Et talia fata` (closing mark joined to `Et`). Units VI.52-53.
- 6.76 `oro. ”Finem dedit ore loquendi`: should read `oro.” Finem…` (closing mark joined to `Finem`). Units VI.76.
The validator will WARN that `t` has 7 opening and 5 closing marks; `l` and `i` are balanced (7/7). Tell me if you want the source corrected and the part re-pinned.
